dict.string: Control Aqara devices and scenes in Agent or Cloud mode

# alfred-aqara
Control Aqara devices and run saved scenes from Alfred. Inspired by Alfred home automation workflows, with the same device-first command style.
The default **Agent mode** uses **Aqara Agent's official cloud API**. Your hub and devices must be registered in Aqara Home. The Mac needs internet access; the hub's IP address and a Home Assistant installation are not required. Availability depends on the devices and account region exposed by Aqara Agent. This is not a direct LAN or Matter controller.
One keyword, `aq`, supports both **Agent** and **Cloud** modes. Run `aq mode` to choose, `aq mode cloud` to enable Cloud, or `aq mode agent` to switch back. Agent is the default, and the choice is remembered. Cloud mode adds supported lock/unlock commands; see [README-cloud.md](README-cloud.md) for authentication, capabilities, and setup. Each mode keeps its own accounts and selected home. Device lists contain only devices from the selected mode; Cloud does not append the Agent inventory.
## Requirements
- macOS with Alfred 5 and a Powerpack license. - Python 3.9 or newer, installed from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/macos/) or Homebrew (`brew install python`). No Python packages are required. - Agent mode: an account that can sign in to [Aqara Agent](https://agent.aqara.com/login). - Cloud mode: an Aqara Home login and a separately imported signing identity; see [Cloud requirements](README-cloud.md#requirements).
## Install and connect
These steps connect the default Agent mode. For Cloud, switch with `aq mode cloud` and follow [the Cloud setup guide](README-cloud.md#connect-cloud-mode).
1. Download [Aqara-0.3.1.alfredworkflow](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-aqara/releases/download/v0.3.1/Aqara-0.3.1.alfredworkflow) and open it to import into Alfred. To build from source, run `python3 workflow-build` and open `dist/Aqara-0.3.1.alfredworkflow`. 2. Type `aq login` in Alfred and press Return. Sign in with your Aqara account. 3. Copy the **aqara_api_key** shown on the page. Type `aq apikey` in Alfred and press Return to paste it into the secure dialog. It is saved in macOS Keychain. The key is never entered in Alfred's search field or stored in the workflow. 4. Run `aq update`. If the account has one home it is selected automatically. With multiple homes, use `aq home` to select one; that selection refreshes its devices and scenes. 5. Type `aq` to browse, or start typing a device, room, or scene name.
macOS may ask you to allow Python to access the Aqara Keychain item. After replacing or updating Python, you may need to allow access again.
## Operating modes and upgrades
`aq mode` shows Agent and Cloud choices and marks the current mode. Select one with Return, or type `aq mode agent` / `aq mode cloud`. The choice persists across Alfred sessions; switching sends no device commands. Commands selected before switching must be selected again afterward.
| Mode | Connection | Controls | | --- | --- | --- | | Agent (default) | Aqara Agent API key | Existing device controls and scenes; locks show status | | Cloud | Aqara Home session and signing identity | Advertised lock/unlock, power, brightness, and color temperature; Exact Agent matches can add controls on the same Cloud row |
Each mode remembers its own accounts, selected home, catalogs, and status preferences. Updates apply to the one workflow, and `aq reinit` resets only the selected mode.
From v0.2.7, run `aq workflow:update` or install the download above. Your Agent connections remain available. Then use `aq mode cloud` and follow [the Cloud guide](README-cloud.md#connect-cloud-mode) if you want Cloud controls. For migration from the earlier parallel workflow, see [Cloud migration](README-cloud.md#upgrading-from-the-parallel-workflow). Changes and validation are in the [v0.3.1 release notes](docs/releases/v0.3.1.md).
## Commands
Command choices have distinct titles such as “Turn on,” “Turn off,” and “Set brightness,” with the device, account, and home in the subtitle. A search matching a single device opens its command list, including when you type only part of its name.
Tab completes the full device name and command. Commands needing a value keep a trailing space so you can continue typing. Mode and colour commands suggest values, and completing a numeric command preserves the value you entered. For example, `aq Desk dim 50` can resolve a unique `Desk Light` and autocomplete to `Desk Light dim 50`. Duplicate device matches require selecting the exact device before a command can run.
Pressing Return on a control sends it to Aqara. Status rows display the device name as the title and the readings as one subtitle line; selecting a status row returns to that device's command list. Use `aq showstatus on` to show the summary above the commands whenever a single device is selected. Names containing spaces, quotes, or shell punctuation are supported.
| Command | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `aq mode` / `aq mode agent` / `aq mode cloud` | View or change the operating mode | | `aq <search>` | Search device names, rooms, device types, and scenes | | `aq <device> status` | Read current state (also works for sensors and hubs) | | `aq <device> on` / `off` | Power controls for lights, switches, outlets, and ACs | | `aq <light> dim 50` | Brightness, 1–100%; use `off` to turn the light off | | `aq <light> color blue` | Set a named color, where supported | | `aq <light> ct 4000` | Color temperature, 2700–6500 K, where supported | | `aq <curtain> open` / `close` / `stop` | Open, close, or pause a curtain/shade | | `aq <curtain> slevel 50` | Opening percentage, 0–100 (100 = fully open) | | `aq <air conditioner> mode cool` | `auto`, `heat`, `cool`, `dry`, or `fan` | | `aq <air conditioner> temp 24` | Temperature in Celsius, 18–30 | | `aq scene <search>` | Search saved scenes; Return requests execution | | `aq update` | Refresh homes, devices, and scenes for the current account | | `aq home` / `aq homes` | Switch between homes across all saved accounts and regions | | `aq home <search>` | Filter homes by home name or account label | | `aq home update` | Discover homes across every saved account | | `aq account` | List saved accounts and regions; select one to restore its last home | | `aq account add <name>` | Save another account/region's API key in a secure dialog | | `aq account rename` | Choose any saved account and enter its new name in a dialog | | `aq account rename <name>` | Rename the current account profile | | `aq showstatus on` / `off` | Automatically show live state on device selection; default off | | `aq login` | Open Aqara's sign-in page | | `aq apikey` | Replace the current account's API key using a secure dialog | | `aq reinit` | Reset saved accounts, credentials, home selections, and catalogs for the selected mode | | `aq workflow:update` | Check GitHub for a newer workflow and start the upgrade | | `aq workflow:autoupdate` | Enable automatic daily update checks (default) | | `aq workflow:noautoupdate` | Disable automatic checks; manual updates remain available |
If a device has the same name as a workflow command, use `aq device <name>`. Devices with duplicate names include room labels; select the exact result to choose a particular device. Multi-channel products may appear as several separately controllable devices.
## Multiple homes, accounts, and regions
`aq home` lists every discovered home across all saved accounts. The current home is marked, and each result includes its account label. Select a home to switch; the workflow remembers that choice. The first result under `aq` shows your current account and home and opens the home picker.
All homes exposed by one account/region share its API key. To connect another account or region:
1. Optionally name the existing connection with `aq account rename Personal`. 2. Run `aq login` and sign in to Aqara Agent with the other account, choosing the region that matches its homes in Aqara Home. Copy its `aqara_api_key`. 3. Run `aq account add US` (or any name you prefer) and paste the key in the secure dialog. The workflow validates it and discovers all homes it exposes. 4. Use `aq home` to choose among homes from both connections. For example, `aq home US` filters by the saved account label.
Each account keeps its own credential, remembered home, device and scene catalogs, and status cache. Switching back to a previously loaded home restores its catalog immediately; use `aq update` to refresh it. A home being selected for the first time loads its catalog from Aqara. Controls and scenes remain scoped to the account and home where they were selected. Homes without saved scenes are supported. If loading a new home's catalog fails, the previous selection and cached data are restored.
To rename a connection that cannot currently load, use `aq account rename`, select that account, and enter a new display name. Renaming does not require switching to that account or contacting Aqara. Account names should contain only a label such as `Work` or `Personal`; API keys go in the separate secure dialog.
Use `aq home update` to discover newly added homes across all saved accounts. Replacing a key with `aq apikey` clears only that connection's home selection and catalogs. Adding another connection preserves the existing connections.
Controls are offered by device family. A specific light may lack color or color temperature support; Aqara can reject a command the hardware does not support. Aqara Agent [explicitly excludes door lock lock/unlock commands](https://github.com/aqara/aqara-agent-skills/blob/main/skills/aqara-agent/SKILL.md#out-of-scope). In Agent mode, door locks show status and an explanation of the unavailable controls. The current API action table also does not document hub security mode controls. Switch to `aq mode cloud` for supported lock controls; see the [Cloud mode guide](README-cloud.md#lock-control). Lock and unlock use declared Cloud command mappings rather than the generic Agent control API. Serialized device status is displayed as readable fields joined in the device's subtitle, for example: `Door: Closed · Lock: Locked · Connection: Online`. Internal remote-control flags are hidden. Copy or Large Type on a status row shows the full summary when the subtitle is too long to fit. Notifications describe the requested action, such as “Turning Desk Light on” or “Setting Desk Light to 50% brightness.” Use `status` to check the device's resulting state. Commands are never retried automatically after a timeout, since they may already have been executed by Aqara.
## Workflow updates
The workflow uses the same bundled Alfred-Workflow updater as [alfred-hubitat](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-hubitat). It checks GitHub Releases in the background once a day while you use `aq`. When a newer stable release is available, an update row appears above the search results. Select it, or run `aq workflow:update` (`aq upgrade` also works). The workflow downloads the release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, bundle identity, and version, then opens Alfred's import dialog. Confirm the upgrade there to finish installing. Releases requiring a newer Alfred version are skipped.
Use `aq workflow:noautoupdate` to turn off automatic checks, and `aq workflow:autoupdate` to turn them back on. `aq update` continues to refresh your Aqara devices, homes, and scenes. Upgrades preserve the selected mode, both modes' saved accounts, home selections, and Keychain credentials. Update checks use GitHub's public API; they do not send Aqara credentials or account data. Updater settings, cached release information, downloads, and logs live under `workflow-updates/` in the workflow data directory, separate from each account's settings.
## Local data
Agent API keys are generic passwords in macOS Keychain with service `com.schwark.aqara`. The original connection uses account `api-key`; added connections use `api-key:<profile-id>`. Home selections and catalogs are stored in Alfred's workflow data directory, outside the installed workflow:
```text ~/Library/Application Support/Alfred/Workflow Data/com.schwark.aqara/ ```
Search uses the local catalog, so typing does not repeatedly query the API. The original connection retains its existing files. Added connections have separate data directories under `profiles/<profile-id>/`; `accounts.json` stores their labels and the active profile, with no credentials. Cloud accounts and catalogs live under `cloud/` and use the separate Keychain service `com.schwark.aqara.cloud`. `mode.json` records the mode preference and selection revision. See [Cloud local data](README-cloud.md#local-data-and-privacy) for the session and signing-identity layout.
Run `aq update` when adding, removing, or renaming devices or scenes. Status requests are cached for five seconds. Controls, scene requests, home changes, and reconnection invalidate status. Replacing the key clears the previous connection's catalogs and home selection. A failed catalog refresh keeps the prior catalog unless the selected home is no longer available.
If `aq update` reports **NoHomesUnderAccount**, Aqara Agent is not returning any homes for the saved credential. Check that the M3 appears in Aqara Home under the same account and region used when signing in to Aqara Agent. Then use `aq login` and `aq apikey` to reconnect. Workflow errors identify the failed operation and known account problems without displaying raw server messages or credentials. Errors appear in Alfred's workflow debugger as well as its notifications.
## Cloud mode
`aq mode cloud` selects the Aqara Home cloud connection in this same workflow. Cloud unlock followed by lock has been verified with U100 and U300 through the shared API. Cloud mode lists only Cloud devices. Verified Agent endpoint matches can supply additional commands on those rows; Agent-only devices stay in Agent mode. Switch back at any time with `aq mode agent`.
See [README-cloud.md](README-cloud.md) for setup, command coverage, multiple accounts and homes, migration from the earlier parallel workflow, and limitations. The [API research notes](docs/aqara-cloud-api-research.md) describe the underlying app protocol. Both modes share one package and update channel.
## Development
```sh python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v /usr/bin/python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v python3 workflow-build ```
The workflow runner finds Python in the standard Apple Silicon Homebrew, Intel Homebrew/python.org, and system locations without depending on a shell profile. The build uses an explicit file allowlist and excludes local data, tests, `.git`, and credentials. Both macOS's Python 3.9 and current Homebrew Python are supported.
The v0.3.1 suite passes 160 offline tests on Python 3.9 and 3.14. Tests cover mode persistence, migration rollback, account/home isolation, stale selections, native capability checks, retained Agent controls, and verified update downloads. The offline suite does not send physical device commands.
`filter.py` renders Alfred results, `command.py` executes selected actions, `common.py` manages Agent requests and the catalog, `cloud_backend.py` adds the Cloud connection, `runtime.py` persists the mode, and `keychain.py` uses the native Security framework. API requests are fixed to the official HTTPS host; redirects are rejected so the bearer key is not forwarded elsewhere.
The [Cloud API report](docs/aqara-cloud-api-research.md) documents signed regional requests, metadata discovery, and tested command behavior. The [hub report](docs/aqara-hub-api-research.md) distinguishes the implemented cloud route from optional LANLink research. These reports and research tools are excluded from the workflow package.
`workflow/` vendors the Python 3 Alfred-Workflow port bundled with Hubitat (Alpynist 2.0.0), originally by Dean Jackson and ported by Arthur Pinheiro. Its MIT license is in `workflow/LICENSE`. Local changes preserve the active Python interpreter and isolated updater directories in background jobs, skip draft releases, and verify GitHub asset checksums and workflow metadata before opening an update. The port's lock files are also closed explicitly for current Python compatibility. No external Python packages are needed.
## API references
The workflow icon is Aqara's logo, sourced from its [official GitHub organization](https://github.com/aqara).
- [Aqara's official Python API client](https://github.com/aqara/aqara-agent-skills/blob/main/skills/aqara-agent/scripts/aqara_open_api.py) - [Aqara's device control action table](https://github.com/aqara/aqara-agent-skills/blob/main/skills/aqara-agent/assets/device_control_action_table.csv) - [Aqara Agent sign-in and remote API documentation](https://github.com/aqara/aqara-mcp-server) - [Alfred Script Filter JSON](https://www.alfredapp.com/help/workflows/inputs/script-filter/json/)
# Aqara Cloud mode
Cloud mode uses the Aqara Home app's cloud API, including lock and unlock on supported endpoints. It is part of the same **Aqara** workflow and uses the same **`aq`** keyword as Agent mode. **Agent is the default.**
```text aq mode Choose Agent or Cloud and see the current mode aq mode cloud Switch to Cloud aq mode agent Switch back to Agent ```
The choice is saved across Alfred sessions. Each mode keeps its own connections, selected account and home, catalogs, and status preferences. Switching modes sends no device commands. A command selected before switching must be selected again afterward.
U100 and U300 cloud unlock followed by lock have been verified with matching reported-state changes. The tested U100 route works through its M3 without phone-to-lock pairing keys. Capability discovery uses Aqara's current endpoint definitions and device metadata rather than bundled drivers for each model.
Cloud mode lists **only devices returned by the Cloud API**. Agent-only devices stay in Agent mode. Importing Agent profiles supplies credentials and fallback metadata; it does not add their devices to the Cloud list.
Native Cloud commands cover lock/unlock, power, brightness, and color temperature where advertised. An exact Agent endpoint match can add fallback controls such as color, curtains, and climate to the same Cloud device row. This mode uses undocumented app APIs and remains experimental.
## Requirements
- macOS with Alfred 5 and a Powerpack license. - Python 3.9 or newer; no additional Python packages are required. - An Aqara Home account with devices in the account's selected region. - A separately obtained app-identity reference for signing Cloud API requests. - An optional Aqara Agent connection for additional controls on exactly matched Cloud endpoints.
The Mac needs internet access. A hub IP address, Home Assistant, an Android emulator, and capture tools are not required at runtime. Cloud mode is a connection option; it does not require a second workflow or keyword.
## Connect Cloud mode
Install [Aqara-0.3.1.alfredworkflow](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-aqara/releases/download/v0.3.1/Aqara-0.3.1.alfredworkflow) from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-aqara/releases/latest). Both modes are included. To build from the repository instead:
```sh python3 workflow-build open dist/Aqara-0.3.1.alfredworkflow ```
1. Run `aq mode cloud`. If the earlier parallel workflow was configured, its saved connections, home links, and signing identity are copied into Cloud mode automatically. Otherwise, run `aq import` before adding Cloud accounts to copy your Agent profiles, cached catalogs, and fallback keys. Agent mode keeps its existing setup. 2. If the signing identity was not migrated, run `aq identity` and select the external `const.py` containing `APPID`, `APPKEY`, `RSA_N`, and `RSA_E`. The reference used during development is [aquara-local at this pinned revision](https://github.com/home-assistant-plugins/aquara-local/blob/4fc274688cd40774307549172c9ae1db073c92ca/custom_components/aquara_local/const.py). Only literal assignments are read; the file is never executed. The imported app identity is saved in Keychain and is excluded from source and packages. 3. For each profile that needs a Cloud session, select it with `aq account`, then run `aq login`. Migrated sessions can be used immediately. Without imported profiles, use `aq login` for the initial connection. Enter the Aqara Home area, two-letter country, username, and password in dialogs. Choose the region used by that account in Aqara Home:
| Aqara Home region | Area | Country | | --- | --- | --- | | India | `SEA` | `IN` | | United States | `US` | `US` | | Other supported areas | `EU`, `CN`, or `KR` | Account country code |
4. Run `aq home` to select a home, then `aq update` to refresh its devices and scenes. Run `aq parity` to inspect native commands and Agent fallback coverage. Repeat login for each imported account/region. 5. If the same home appears separately from Agent and Cloud discovery, select its Agent entry and run `aq home link` to choose the Cloud counterpart. Run `aq update` afterward. Use `aq home unlink` to remove that association.
The account password is used once for sign-in and then discarded. Only the returned session and routing fields are saved in Keychain. Sessions are not refreshed automatically; run `aq login` again if a session expires or is rejected. macOS may ask you to allow Python to access the Keychain items.
## Upgrading from the parallel workflow
Install the unified Aqara workflow into the existing `aq` entry, then run `aq mode cloud`. On the first switch, the workflow copies the earlier parallel setup's profiles, catalogs, home links, sessions, and signing identity into the new Cloud data directory and Keychain service. Existing Cloud data is not overwritten, and a failed migration removes its newly copied credentials. The earlier setup remains available for recovery.
Migrated sessions can be used immediately; run `aq login` only when reconnecting an expired or rejected session. Do not run `aq import` after migration, since it is only for an unconfigured Cloud mode. Once the unified setup works, disable or remove the earlier parallel workflow in Alfred to retire its old keyword. The workflow migrates data; it does not remove another installed workflow.
## Daily use
These commands use the selected mode. Lock controls and Cloud setup commands are available in Cloud mode.
Type `aq` to browse, or type part of a device, room, or scene name. A search matching one device opens its commands. Choices have distinct titles such as “Turn on,” “Turn off,” “Lock,” and “Unlock”; the subtitle identifies the device and home. Status appears as a readable subtitle instead of raw JSON.
Tab completes device names, commands, and suggested values. Commands needing a value keep a trailing space so you can continue typing. Duplicate device names require selecting the exact result before running a command. Use `aq device <name>` when a device name conflicts with a workflow command.
| Command | Behavior | | --- | --- | | `aq mode` / `aq mode agent` / `aq mode cloud` | View or change the operating mode | | `aq <search>` | Find devices, rooms, types, and scenes | | `aq <device> status` | Read the current reported state | | `aq <lock> lock` / `unlock` | Request lock control where the endpoint advertises it | | `aq <device> on` / `off` | Power control where supported | | `aq <light> dim 50` | Set brightness | | `aq <light> ct 4000` | Set color temperature in kelvin | | `aq <light> color blue` | Set color through Agent fallback | | `aq <curtain> open` / `close` / `stop` / `slevel 50` | Curtain controls through Agent fallback | | `aq <air conditioner> mode cool` / `temp 24` | Climate controls through Agent fallback | | `aq scene <search>` | Find a saved scene; Return requests execution | | `aq showstatus on` / `off` | Show or hide live status above a device's commands | | `aq update` | Refresh the selected account's homes and current catalog | | `aq parity` | Inspect native capability discovery and retained Agent coverage |
Existing scenes retain their Agent execution route. Additional Cloud scenes use the app's scene API; that request construction has been verified in app code, but live execution remains unverified.
Notifications describe the requested action. Use `status` to check the resulting reported state. Browsing, import, refresh, and coverage inspection do not issue device writes. A failed native write is never retried through Agent.
## Multiple homes, accounts, and regions
`aq home` lists homes across saved accounts and regions, with account labels to distinguish them. Each connection remembers its selected home and catalogs. Selecting another home restores or loads its catalog; a failed switch restores the previous selection.
- `aq account add <label>` creates another connection and prompts for its Cloud login. Use a separate profile for each account/region combination. - `aq account` switches profiles; `aq account rename` lets you choose and rename a profile without connecting to it. `aq account rename <label>` renames the current profile. - `aq apikey` adds or replaces the selected profile's Agent fallback key, obtained from [Aqara Agent](https://agent.aqara.com/login). Run `aq update` after connecting it. - `aq home <search>` filters homes by name or account label. `aq home update` discovers homes across all saved connections.
Home links are explicit when API IDs differ; similar names never create a link automatically. Cloud devices use their Cloud names and identifiers. A fallback is attached only by an exact device ID or a unique returned endpoint identifier matching the Agent endpoint ID; names never attach controls. Unmatched Agent devices remain accessible with `aq mode agent`. Different Cloud devices with the same name use room labels, and multi-endpoint devices can have separate entries. Existing mixed caches are filtered automatically, including cached catalogs restored when switching homes.
Matched devices keep their original Agent commands. Native power, brightness, and color-temperature controls are used when advertised and compatible with the requested value. Otherwise the existing Agent route can be selected before the write. A failure never triggers a second transport automatically.
## Lock control
Select the exact lock and choose **Unlock** or **Lock**. Both use the same regional cloud command route; the U100's tested path reaches it through its M3. No direct LAN connection is required.
Commands are offered only when Aqara's endpoint metadata declares the common DoorLock commands. Matter devices use their device capabilities; Zigbee/hub devices use current server definitions confirmed by a live lock-state read. Execution rechecks the model, home, endpoint, and capabilities. Unknown capabilities remain read-only.
If the device metadata says a remote-control password is configured, a hidden dialog asks for that separate **device password**, not your Aqara account password. Leave it empty if none is configured. It is used for that request and is not saved. Cancel sends no command. A rejection or timeout is not retried.
Live tests sent one Unlock followed by one Lock to each tested U100 and U300. Both requests were accepted, and fresh reads reported the requested states. Those tests establish cloud acceptance and status readback; mechanical movement was not independently observed. Other device/firmware combinations have not been verified. Details are in the [Cloud API notes](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-aqara/blob/main/docs/aqara-cloud-api-research.md) and [M3 hub investigation](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-aqara/blob/main/docs/aqara-hub-api-research.md).
## Updates
Both modes share the same updater and stable GitHub Releases with `Aqara-*` assets. The earlier parallel packages are ignored. Update checks run daily while using either mode; the chosen mode and each mode's connections survive upgrades.
- `aq workflow:update` checks for an update and opens Alfred's import dialog after verifying the download's SHA-256, bundle identity, and version. - `aq workflow:autoupdate` enables automatic checks, the default. - `aq workflow:noautoupdate` disables automatic checks.
Complete an upgrade in Alfred's import dialog. Saved accounts, home links, and Keychain credentials live outside the installed workflow and survive upgrades. `aq update` refreshes devices and scenes; it does not upgrade the workflow.
## Local data and privacy
The workflow bundle is `com.schwark.aqara`. Cloud credentials use the separate Keychain service `com.schwark.aqara.cloud`, with accounts `connection:<profile-id>` and `app-identity` for the signing identity. Cloud account labels, catalogs, home links, and five-second status caches live under:
```text ~/Library/Application Support/Alfred/Workflow Data/com.schwark.aqara/cloud/ ```
`aq reinit` resets only the selected mode's connections, credentials, home selections, and catalogs. In Cloud mode the signing identity remains in Keychain for reconnecting accounts. Agent mode's data stays in the parent workflow data directory, and `mode.json` stores the operating-mode choice.
Packages use an explicit file allowlist. They contain no saved accounts, home/device records, app constants, credentials, APKs, or traffic captures. Research tools are excluded from the workflow; see the [Cloud API research notes](https://github.com/schwark/alfred-aqara/blob/main/docs/aqara-cloud-api-research.md) for protocol details and read-only capture tools.
Search devices and scenes, or connect your account
Keyword used to search Aqara devices and scenes.
